newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures steady to lower ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures steady to lower ahead of data.

text.p: U.S. debt futures were steady to lower in early trading ahead of October industrial output and capacity use data, and before the University of Michigan consumer sentiment index.
Traders said Thursday's run in December Treasury bonds to a fresh nine-month high may have been a bit overdone.

"It seemed like it was more short-covering when you got through key levels on Thursday," one debt trader said. Traders said 115-2/32, 115-9/32 and 115-11/32 were resistance levels to watch early today.
One T-bond futures trader noted that Friday's early action mimicked Thursday's trade, when the market traded lower early but then rallied later in the day.

"There were sellers right on the open, they knocked it down to 114-31/32 and (one firm) bought 700 contracts at even to 115-2/32 and now it just sits," he said. He said a decisive rejection of the 114-31/32 low could push the market to challenge resistance levels.
He said the impending Dec T-bond and note options expiration could see the market drift higher heading into midday, as well.

March Eurodollars were unchanged in early trading at 94.49, still stuck in their recent range. Euros remain in a neutral market situation, said John Nyhoff, chief economist at Mistubishi Financial Futures. "You need more information to decide if the teeter totter is swinging up or swinging down," he said.
Traders noted that U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin was scheduled to speak at 0800 CST/1400 GMT.
Industrial production and capacity use, due at 0815 CST/1415 GMT, was forecast unchanged and at 83.0 percent, respectively.
University of Michigan's November preliminary consumer sentiment index was forecast at 95.7 compared with the 96.5 October final. That index will be released at 0900 CDT/1500 GMT.
At 0802 CST/1402 GMT, Dec T-bonds were down 5 basis points at 115-4/32, muni-bonds fell 8/32 to 117-9/32, March Euros were down 1 basis point to 94.48 and Dec 10-year notes lost 3/32 to 110-24/32.
